about.title: About
about.lead: I am looking for a junior cybersecurity engineer or consultant position, primarily in Luxembourg, the French border area and the Metz / Thionville area.

blocks.title: Background
blocks.text: Technological baccalauréat (STI2D), a two-year BTS SIO diploma at EFREI, then a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science and a Master's degree in Cybersecurity at Ynov Paris (French RNCP 40897 qualification, “Cybersecurity Expert”, level 7). Since November 2025, apprenticeship at Novastill, an IT services company specialising in cybersecurity and managed services.

blocks.title: Positioning
blocks.text: Configuration auditing, infrastructure security and managed services: I work on multi-client production environments, from reviewing a firewall rule set to operating a high-availability web filtering platform, including incident troubleshooting and deliverable writing.

blocks.title: Advisory posture
blocks.text: I talk directly to the client's stakeholders — CISO, IT director, data protection officer — and to the vendors, and I turn a technical finding into an actionable recommendation, in a report or a written summary.

blocks.title: Automation, as a complement
blocks.text: Scripting is not my core discipline. I use Python, Bash and PowerShell as automation and troubleshooting tools: parsing a configuration export, collecting logs, checking a configuration before rollout. My GitHub repositories are small auditing and troubleshooting tools written in that spirit.

methods.title: Methods and tools
methods.intro: How I run an audit or troubleshooting assignment, and with what.

process.text: Retrieval of the configuration export (Forcepoint SMC, FortiOS backup, pfSense) following a documented collection procedure.
Rebuilding the rule table: objects, groups, VDOMs, sub-policies, interfaces.
Spotting permissive, obsolete, disabled, unlogged or undocumented rules; checking the logging setup.
Exposure of sensitive services, clear-text protocols, wide ranges, associated risks and business context.
Audit report with rationalisation and hardening recommendations, presented to the CISO.

projects.title: Projects
projects.intro: Auditing, troubleshooting and learning tools published on GitHub. They extend situations met on assignments; the code stays deliberately simple and dependency-free, and is not an end in itself.

items.name: fw-audit
items.objective: Automatically spot classic misconfigurations in a firewall rule set.
items.problem: Reading several hundred rules by hand is slow and error-prone. The tool applies five checks — “any → any” rule, sensitive service exposed to any source (exact port or a range containing it), clear-text protocol, wide port range, undocumented rule — with a severity and a recommendation for each finding.
items.results: 18 passing unit tests. Also reads the fortigate-policy-parser CSV export directly (disabled policies skipped, FortiOS services translated into ports, findings tied to the policy id). Validated on a 9-rule sample set and 5 FortiGate policies.
items.skills: Firewall rule analysis, risk qualification, recommendations.

items.name: fortigate-policy-parser
items.objective: Flatten a FortiGate backup into a rule table usable for an audit.
items.problem: A FortiOS export runs to thousands of lines. The tool rebuilds VDOMs, objects and groups, exports the policies to CSV and qualifies the rules: any → any accept, disabled rules, accept without logging, unnamed rules.
items.results: 12 passing unit tests. --resolve option: addresses as subnets and services as protocol/ports, read directly by fw-audit. On the sample configuration: 5 policies, 3 findings. IPv4 policies only.
items.skills: FortiGate auditing, reading FortiOS configuration, rule mapping.

items.name: haproxy-audit
items.objective: Review an HAProxy configuration with an auditor's eye: exposure, TLS, logging, hardening, and the ability to survive an outage.
items.problem: An unauthenticated stats page, an enabled stats admin, TLS 1.0 still accepted or a node without a health check stay invisible until an incident. The tool splits haproxy.cfg into sections, applies defaults inheritance and reports 20 security and high-availability checks with a severity and a recommendation.
items.results: 13 passing unit tests; on the sample configuration: 1 critical, 3 high and 6 medium findings; the hardened version reports nothing. Static analysis of a single file, ACLs not interpreted.
items.skills: Infrastructure security, high availability, configuration analysis, recommendations.

items.name: pac-check
items.objective: Validate a PAC file before rollout, like any other configuration.
items.problem: A badly written exclusion or a misordered failover chain breaks an access path or high availability, and you only notice once the file is deployed. The tool evaluates FindProxyForURL outside the browser and compares the result with an expectations file.
items.results: 6/6 expectations verified on the sample PAC; 7 passing automated tests (node:test). Does not reproduce the https URL truncation performed by browsers.
items.skills: Web filtering, high availability, proxy operations.

items.name: log-secret-scanner
items.objective: Detect clear-text secrets in logs and configuration files, without ever displaying them.
items.problem: A service that logs a password or an Authorization header exposes that secret to anyone reading the logs and to the collection platform. Ten patterns, one severity per pattern, already-masked values ignored, .gz archives read as a stream.
items.results: 11 passing unit tests; 6 redacted findings on the sample log. Pattern-based detection only, no entropy analysis.
items.skills: Operational security, log management, reporting and remediation.

items.name: osint-toolkit
items.objective: Measure an organisation's public exposure passively, ahead of an audit.
items.problem: Eight commands: DNS over HTTPS, raw-socket WHOIS, IP geolocation, TLS certificate inspection, HTTP security header scoring, subdomains through Certificate Transparency, username presence, email header analysis. No intrusive probing of the target.
items.results: Network commands validated manually on public domains; 6 unit tests on the local modules (email headers, HTTP header grading). Relies on free third-party services.
items.skills: Passive reconnaissance, header analysis, phishing awareness.

items.name: pwned-check
items.objective: Check whether a password is compromised without ever exposing it.
items.problem: Have I Been Pwned's k-anonymity model reimplemented: local SHA-1 hashing, only the first five characters of the digest are sent, final comparison happens locally, response padded through the Add-Padding header.
items.results: Hidden input and distinct exit codes (not found, compromised, error). One password at a time; no automated tests.

items.name: pc-tools
items.objective: Apply safe-operations reflexes — dry run by default, explicit destructive action — to file administration tasks.
items.problem: Duplicate detection by SHA-256 digest, largest-files search, bulk renaming. Deletion requires --delete, renaming requires --apply; name collisions are listed without overwriting any data.
items.results: Used daily; 9 passing unit tests (duplicates, largest files, rename plan, collisions). No recycle bin: a deletion is final.
items.skills: Systems administration, access error handling, guard rails.

items.name: Active Directory infrastructure
items.objective: Deploy and administer an Active Directory domain end to end.
items.problem: User and Group Policy management, workstation imaging and deployment through MDT and WDS.
items.results: Practical grounding in directory services and endpoint management, later reused during the apprenticeship on domain-join and authentication topics.

items.name: Labs and CTFs
items.objective: Keep my understanding of attack techniques current, to assess an infrastructure's exposure correctly.
items.problem: Regular practice on lab and CTF platforms: web pentesting, system exploitation, forensics, steganography, privilege escalation.
items.results: Ongoing practice, with no ranking or score put forward.
items.skills: Offensive culture applied to defensive auditing.
